shlokas.english_draft: Om! O Devas, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O worshipful ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. May we, enjoying with firm limbs and bodies, live the full span of life allotted by the Devas. May Indra of ancient fame grant us welfare! May Pushan, the all-knowing, grant us welfare! May Tarksya (Garuda), the protector from harm, grant us welfare! May Brihaspati grant us welfare! Om Peace, Peace, Peace! Om, salutations to Brahman.

shlokas.text: प्रथममुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ ॐ ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता । स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह
shlokas.english_draft: First Mundaka, First Khanda. Om. Brahma was the first of the Devas to arise—the creator of the universe and the protector of the world. He taught the knowledge of Brahman (Brahma-vidya), the foundation of all knowledge, to his eldest son Atharva.

shlokas.text: अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माऽथर्वा तं पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम् । स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवाहाय प्राह भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम्
shlokas.english_draft: That knowledge of Brahman which Brahma imparted to Atharva, Atharva of old taught to Angir. Angir taught it to Satyavaha of the lineage of Bharadvaja, and Bharadvaja transmitted it in succession (para-vara) to Angiras.

shlokas.text: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति
shlokas.english_draft: Shaunaka, the great householder, having approached Sage Angiras in the prescribed manner, asked: 'Venerable Sir, what is that by knowing which all this universe becomes known?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाच । द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च
shlokas.english_draft: To him Sage Angiras replied: 'Two kinds of knowledge are to be known, as declared by the knowers of Brahman—the lower knowledge (apara vidya) and the higher knowledge (para vidya).'

shlokas.text: तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति । अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Of these, the lower knowledge consists of the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharvaveda, phonetics (Shiksha), ritual codes (Kalpa), grammar (Vyakarana), etymology (Nirukta), metrics (Chhandas), and astronomy (Jyotisha). But the higher knowledge is that by which the Imperishable (Akshara) is realized.'

shlokas.text: यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्ण- मचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम् । नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः
shlokas.english_draft: 'That which is imperceptible, ungraspable, without origin, without attributes, without eyes or ears, without hands or feet, eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, extremely subtle, immutable—that is what the wise behold as the source of all beings.'

shlokas.text: यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति । यथा सतः पुरुषात्केशलोमानि तथाऽक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'As a spider projects and retracts its web, as plants sprout from the earth, and as hair grows on the head and body of a living person, so from the Imperishable (Akshara) arises this entire universe.'

shlokas.text: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते । अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Through tapas (creative contemplation), Brahman expands; from That food (unmanifest cosmic matter) is produced; from food comes Prana (life-force), mind, truth, the worlds, and in rituals, immortality (the fruits of action).'

shlokas.text: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः । तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायते
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him who is omniscient (knowing all in general) and all-wise (knowing everything in detail), whose tapas consists of pure knowledge—from Him is born this conditioned Brahman, as well as name, form, and food.'

shlokas.text: ॥ इति मुण्डकोपनिषदि प्रथममुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ ॥ प्रथममुण्डके द्वितीयः खण्डः ॥ तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा संततानि । तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके
shlokas.english_draft: Thus ends the First Khanda of the First Mundaka. First Mundaka, Second Khanda. 'This is the truth: The sacrificial rituals which the wise seers perceived in the Vedic mantras were expanded in diverse ways in the Treta age. Perform them constantly, O lovers of truth; this is your path to the world of good deeds.'

shlokas.text: यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने । तदाऽऽज्यभागावन्तरेणाऽऽहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत्
shlokas.english_draft: 'When the flame flickers, the fire being fully ignited, one should offer the oblations with faith between the two portions of melted butter (ajya-bhaga).'

shlokas.text: (प्रतिपादयेच्छ्रद्धया हुतम्) यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमास- मचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितं च । अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुत- मासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान् हिनस्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'If a man's Agnihotra sacrifice is unassisted by the new-moon (Darsha), full-moon (Paurnamasa), four-monthly (Chaturmasya), autumnal harvest (Agrayana) rites, is devoid of guests, unoffered, without Vaishwadeva rite, or performed contrary to prescribed rules, it destroys his worlds up to the seventh generation.'

shlokas.text: काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Kali (the black), Karali (the terrifying), Manojava (swift as thought), Sulohita (deep red), Sudhumravarna (smoke-colored), Sphulingini (sparkling), and Vishwaruchi (all-glowing)—these are the seven flickering tongues of fire.'

shlokas.text: एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् । तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र (तन्नयन्त्येताः) देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Whoever performs rituals when these flames are shining, offering oblations at the proper time, these oblations as rays of the sun carry him to where the supreme lord of the Devas resides.'

shlokas.text: एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति । प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Saying "Come, come!", the luminous oblations carry the sacrificer upon the rays of the sun, praising him with pleasing words: "This is your holy world of Brahman, earned by your good deeds."'

shlokas.text: प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म । एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Frail indeed are these boats of sacrifice, eighteen in number, upon which rests this lower karma. The deluded who rejoice in this as the supreme good undergo old age and death again and again.'

shlokas.text: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Existing in the midst of ignorance (avidya), considering themselves wise and learned, the deluded wander about afflicted, like the blind led by the blind.'

shlokas.text: अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः । यत्कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागा- त्तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Living in varied states of ignorance, the immature delude themselves thinking, "We have achieved our life's goal!" Because ritualists do not comprehend the truth due to attachment, they become miserable and fall from heaven when the merit of their works is exhausted.'

shlokas.text: इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः । नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Imagining sacrifices and works of public utility (ishta-purta) to be the highest good, these deluded ones know nothing higher. Having enjoyed the reward of their good deeds on the high summit of heaven, they re-enter this world or an even lower one.'

shlokas.text: तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्ष्यचर्यां चरन्तः । सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा
shlokas.english_draft: 'But those who practice austerity (tapas) and faith (shraddha) in the forest, tranquil, learned, living on alms, depart stainless through the gate of the sun to where resides that immortal, imperishable Purusha.'

shlokas.text: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्मचितान् ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन । तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Having examined the worlds acquired through karma, let a Brahmana attain detachment (nirveda). What is uncreated (Brahman) cannot be produced by action. To know That, he must, with sacrificial fuel in hand, approach a Guru who is well-versed in the Vedas (Shrotriya) and established in Brahman (Brahmanishtha).'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक् प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय । येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच तां तत्त्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'To him who has thus approached properly, whose mind is tranquil and senses calmed, the wise teacher imparts in its full truth that knowledge of Brahman (Brahma-vidya) by which one knows the true, imperishable Purusha.'

shlokas.text: द्वितीय मुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ तदेतत्सत्यं यथा सुदीप्तात्पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः । तथाऽक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापियन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: Second Mundaka, First Khanda. 'This is the truth: As from a blazing fire thousands of sparks of identical nature spring forth, so, O gentle one, from the Imperishable (Akshara) originate diverse beings and unto It they return.'

shlokas.text: दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः । अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात्परतः परः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Luminous, formless is the Purusha; He exists both outside and inside, unborn, without Prana, without mind, pure, higher than the highest Imperishable (Maya).'

shlokas.text: एतस्माज्जायते प्राणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च । खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him originate Prana, mind, all the sense faculties, ether (akasha), air, fire, water, and the earth, which supports all.'

shlokas.text: अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च वेदाः । वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
shlokas.english_draft: 'Fire (heaven) is His head; the sun and moon His eyes; the directions His ears; the revealed Vedas His speech; air His breath; the cosmos His heart; from His feet the earth is born. He is indeed the inner Self (Antaratman) of all beings.'

shlokas.text: तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् । पुमान् रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात्संप्रसूताः
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him comes the fire whose fuel is the sun; from the moon comes rain (Parjanya); from rain herbs sprout on earth; man casts seed into woman—thus many offspring are produced from the Purusha.'

shlokas.text: तस्मादृचः साम यजूꣳषि दीक्षा यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च । संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him originate the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, consecrations (diksha), sacrifices, rituals, sacrificial gifts (dakshina), the year, the sacrificer, and the worlds where the moon purifies and where the sun shines.'

shlokas.text: तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा संप्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयाꣳसि । प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him also the various Devas are born, as well as Sadhyas, humans, beasts, birds, Prana and Apana, rice and barley, austerity, faith, truth, celibacy (brahmacharya), and rules of conduct.'

shlokas.text: सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मा- त्सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः । सप्त इमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him originate the seven Pranas (sense organs), seven flames, seven fuels, seven oblations, and these seven worlds in which the Pranas move, placed seven by seven in the cave of the heart.'

shlokas.text: अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वेऽस्मा- त्स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः । अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा
shlokas.english_draft: 'From Him originate all oceans and mountains; from Him flow rivers of every form; from Him come all herbs and the essential sap by which the inner Self remains seated within the elements.'

shlokas.text: पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम् । एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य
shlokas.english_draft: 'The Purusha alone is all this universe—karma, tapas, Brahman, the supreme immortal. O gentle one, he who knows Him hidden in the cave of the heart unties the knot of ignorance (avidya-granthi) right here in this life.'

shlokas.text: ॥ इति मुण्डकोपनिषदि द्वितीयमुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ ॥ द्वितीय मुण्डके द्वितीयः खण्डः ॥ आविः संनिहितं गुहाचरं नाम महत्पदमत्रैतत्समर्पितम् । एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम्
shlokas.english_draft: Thus ends the First Khanda of the Second Mundaka. Second Mundaka, Second Khanda. 'Manifest, near, dwelling in the cave of the heart, named the Great Abode—in It is centered all that moves, breathes, and winks. Know It as existing and non-existing, adorable, beyond the comprehension of creatures, the supreme among all.'

shlokas.text: यदर्चिमद्यदणुभ्योऽणु च यस्मिँल्लोका निहिता लोकिनश्च । तदेतदक्षरं ब्रह्म स प्राणस्तदु वाङ्मनः तदेतत्सत्यं तदमृतं तद्वेद्धव्यं सोम्य विद्धि
shlokas.english_draft: 'That which is luminous, subtler than the subtle, in which are fixed all the worlds and their inhabitants—that is the imperishable Brahman. That is Prana, speech, and mind. That is the Truth, That is Immortality. That is to be pierced (targeted), O gentle one; pierce It!'

shlokas.text: धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं शरं ह्युपासानिशितं संधयीत । (संदधीत) आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि
shlokas.english_draft: 'Taking as a bow the great weapon of the Upanishads, place upon it the arrow sharpened by meditation. Drawing it with a mind absorbed in That, know, O gentle one, that imperishable target!'

shlokas.text: प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Om is the bow, the Atman (Self) is the arrow, and Brahman is called the target. It must be pierced with undivided attention; one should become one with It, just like the arrow becomes one with its target.'

shlokas.text: यस्मिन् द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः । तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः
shlokas.english_draft: 'He in whom heaven, earth, and inter-space are woven, along with the mind and all the Pranas—know Him alone as the one Atman, and discard all other speech. This is the bridge to Immortality.'

shlokas.text: अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः । स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः । ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Where the subtle channels (nadis) meet like spokes at the hub of a chariot wheel, there He moves within, manifesting in manifold ways. Meditate on Om as the Atman. May welfare be yours as you cross to the shore beyond darkness!'

shlokas.text: (पराय) यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्यैष महिमा भुवि । दिव्ये ब्रह्मपुरे ह्येष व्योम्न्यात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ (संप्रतिष्ठितः) मनोमयः प्राणशरीरनेता प्रतिष्ठितोऽन्ने हृदयं संनिधाय । तद्विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीरा आनन्दरूपममृतं यद्विभाति
shlokas.english_draft: 'He who is omniscient, all-wise, whose glory is manifested in the world, resides in the divine city of Brahman in the space of the heart. He consists of mind, leads the body and Prana, and is established in food, abiding in the heart. By realizing Him through wisdom, the wise behold That which shines forth as bliss and immortality.'

shlokas.text: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे
shlokas.english_draft: 'The knot of the heart is unloosed, all doubts are dispelled, and all one's karmas are destroyed when He, the Supreme and the Immanent (Para-Avara), is seen.'

shlokas.text: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम् । तच्छुभ्रं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिस्तद्यदात्मविदो विदुः
shlokas.english_draft: 'In the supreme golden sheath abides the stainless, partless Brahman. That is pure, the Light of lights, which the knowers of the Atman know.'

shlokas.text: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति
shlokas.english_draft: 'The sun does not shine there, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine, how much less this fire! Everything shines after Him who shines; by His light all this is illuminated.'

shlokas.text: ब्रह्मैवेदममृतं पुरस्ताद्ब्रह्म पश्चाद्ब्रह्म दक्षिणतश्चोत्तरेण । अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Brahman alone is this immortal entity in front, Brahman behind, Brahman to the right and to the left, above and below extended; Brahman alone is this entire magnificent universe.'

shlokas.text: तृतीय मुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति
shlokas.english_draft: Third Mundaka, First Khanda. 'Two birds, bound to each other in close friendship, perch on the self-same tree. Of these two, one eats the sweet fruit, while the other looks on without eating.'

shlokas.text: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नो- ऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीश- मस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Seated on the same tree, the individual soul (jiva) sinks in grief, deluded by its own helplessness. But when it beholds the other—the worshipful Lord—and His glory, it becomes freed from sorrow.'

shlokas.text: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् । तदा विद्वान् पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति
shlokas.english_draft: 'When the seer beholds the golden-hued Creator, the Lord, the Purusha, the source of Brahman, then, wise and shaking off merit and sin, stainless, he attains supreme equality.'

shlokas.text: प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावा- नेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Verily, He is Prana shining forth through all beings. The wise one who knows Him does not indulge in useless debate. Delighting in the Self, sporting in the Self, engaged in spiritual action—he is the foremost among the knowers of Brahman.'

shlokas.text: सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् । अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः
shlokas.english_draft: 'This Atman is to be attained by truth, by tapas, by right knowledge, and by constant celibacy (brahmacharya). Resplendent and pure, He resides within the body, whom the ascetics with eradicated blemishes behold.'

shlokas.text: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं (जयति) सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Truth alone triumphs, not falsehood. By truth is paved the divine path (Devayana) by which the sages, free from desires, ascend to where lies the supreme treasure of Truth.'

shlokas.text: बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्माच्च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति । दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यत्स्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Vast, divine, of unthinkable form, subtler than the subtle, It shines forth. Farther than the far, yet right here near at hand, It is perceived by seers hidden right here in the cave of the heart.'

shlokas.text: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा । ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्व- स्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः
shlokas.english_draft: 'It is not grasped by the eye, nor by speech, nor by other senses, nor by tapas or rituals. When one's intellect is purified by the light of knowledge, then through meditation one beholds the partless Brahman.'

shlokas.text: एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश । प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा
shlokas.english_draft: 'This subtle Atman is to be known by the mind into which Prana has entered fivefold. The entire mind of creatures is pervaded by the Pranas; when the mind is purified, this Atman reveals Himself.'

shlokas.text: यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् । तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामां- स्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेद्भूतिकामः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Whatever world a man of purified mind envisions in his mind and whatever desires he cherishes, he wins that world and obtains those desires. Therefore, let one who desires prosperity honor the knower of the Atman.'

shlokas.text: ॥ इति मुण्डकोपनिषदि तृतीयमुण्डके प्रथमः खण्डः ॥ ॥ तृतीयमुण्डके द्वितीयः खण्डः ॥ स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् । उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः
shlokas.english_draft: Thus ends the First Khanda of the Third Mundaka. Third Mundaka, Second Khanda. 'He knows that supreme abode of Brahman wherein the universe rests and shines brightly. The wise who, free from worldly desires, worship the Purusha, transcend this seed of rebirth.'

shlokas.text: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः
shlokas.english_draft: 'He who entertains desires, dwelling on them, is born here and there on account of those desires. But for him whose desires are fulfilled and who has realized the Atman, all desires dissolve right here in this life.'

shlokas.text: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्य- स्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'This Atman cannot be attained by instruction, nor by intellect, nor by much hearing. He whom the Atman chooses, by him the Atman is attained; to him this Atman reveals His true nature.'

shlokas.text: (आत्मा वृणुते) नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वां- स्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम
shlokas.english_draft: 'This Atman cannot be attained by one devoid of strength, nor through carelessness, nor by tapas without proper renunciation. But the wise man who strives through these proper means, his soul enters the abode of Brahman.'

shlokas.text: संप्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः । ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Having attained Him, the sages—satisfied with knowledge, self-realized, free from passion, and serene—attain the all-pervading Brahman on all sides and, united in Self, enter into everything.'

shlokas.text: वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः । ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे
shlokas.english_draft: 'Having well ascertained the truth through the wisdom of Vedanta, and having purified their minds through the yoga of renunciation, those ascetics at the supreme end of time, liberated in the world of Brahman, become supreme immortals.'

shlokas.text: गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु । कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा परेऽव्यये सर्वे एकीभवन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Their fifteen constituent parts return to their foundations, and all their senses into their corresponding deities; their karma and the intellect-bound soul (Vijnanamaya Atman) all become one in the supreme, imperishable Reality.'

shlokas.text: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रे- ऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'As flowing rivers disappear into the ocean, casting off name and form, so the wise person, liberated from name and form, reaches the divine Purusha, who is higher than the highest.'

shlokas.text: स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति । तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति
shlokas.english_draft: 'He who knows that supreme Brahman becomes Brahman Himself. In his lineage, none ignorant of Brahman is born. He crosses beyond sorrow, crosses beyond sin, and freed from the knots of the heart, becomes immortal.'

shlokas.text: तदेतदृचाऽभ्युक्तम् । क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः । तेषामेवैतां ब्रह्मविद्यां वदेत शिरोव्रतं विधिवद्यैस्तु चीर्णम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'This is declared by the Vedic verse: To those who perform rituals, are versed in the Vedas, established in Brahman, offer oblations with faith to the single Rishi (Ekarshi), and who have duly observed the vow of the head (Shiro-vrata)—to them alone should this knowledge of Brahman be taught.'

shlokas.text: तदेतत्सत्यमृषिरङ्गिराः पुरोवाच नैतदचीर्णव्रतोऽधीते । नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः
shlokas.english_draft: 'This is the truth declared in ancient times by the seer Angiras. One who has not fulfilled the vow does not study this. Salutations to the supreme seers! Salutations to the supreme seers!'
